correctness.rationale: For arbitrary n>=1, the Tits product takes the left nonzero comparison sign and otherwise the right comparison sign. Opposite nonzero signs are the exact obstruction to commutation. A pairwise commuting family has a common chamber refinement, so maximal cliques are precisely the consecutive-block coarsenings of each permutation (n! cliques of size 2^(n-1)); shared-prefix cuts yield overlap 2^d and indecomposable-permutation spectrum. On each block A_i of a fixed face, beta restricts to one arbitrary ordered partition; between consecutive A_i restrictions there is one binary merge choice, giving |C(alpha)|=2^(b-1)*product F_|A_i| and degree minus one. Counting nonempty subsets of r tuple labels on each cut gives T_{n,r}=sum_b b! S(n,b)(2^r-1)^(b-1). Stirling inversion gives each clique-size count; pole analysis of its EGF yields fixed-r asymptotic. An independently written checker generated all ordered partitions by surjections and compared products and centralizer counts for n=1..4: faces 1,3,13,75 and commuting ordered pairs 1,7,73,1015. Checks substantiate but do not replace the unrestricted combinatorial proof. n=1 identity and n=2 exceptional universality handled.
